cards.topic: 10.11. Klausur 1 — Textbook exam cases (possession, acquiring ownership)
cards.front: [Textbook Exercise 1, Ch. XIII] Helen lends Drusus her horse for a day; Drusus puts it in his stable, where Lunius steals it during the night. The next day Lunius sells it to Klio; a week later Klio's slave fetches it on her orders. Who possesses the horse at each stage?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exercise 1, Kap. XIII] Helen leiht Drusus ihr Pferd für einen Tag; Drusus stellt es in seinen Stall, wo Lunius es nachts stiehlt. Am nächsten Tag verkauft Lunius es an Klio; eine Woche später holt Klios Sklave es auf ihren Befehl. Wer besitzt das Pferd in den einzelnen Stadien?
cards.back:
1. Helen: proprietary possessor (ANIMUS + CORPUS).
2. Loan: Drusus becomes detentor (immediate natural possession, ANIMUS REM ALTERI HABENDI); Helen retains mediate proprietary possession.
3. Theft: Lunius acquires possession originally (FURTUM), Helen and Drusus lose their positions.
4. Sale to Klio: changes nothing as regards possession (sale ≠ possession).
5. Collection: Klio acquires possession ANIMO NOSTRO CORPORE ALIENO (IUSSUM to the slave) — derivatively from Lunius.
• Method: proceed chronologically, state the elements, subsume.

cards.topic: 10.11. Klausur 1 — Textbook exam cases (possession, acquiring ownership)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 3] Cato inherits a country house from his aunt and in January sells Nike a bed made of thuja wood and a silver table. Nike has both collected by her slave Ganymed (PECULIUM, furniture shop) and taken to the warehouse. In March of the following year Agamemnon demands the return of the silver table, which he had given to the aunt for safekeeping. Who owns (a) the bed, (b) the table?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 3] Cato erbt von seiner Tante ein Landhaus und verkauft im Januar Nike ein Bett aus Thujaholz und einen Silbertisch. Nike lässt beides von ihrem Sklaven Ganymed (PECULIUM, Möbelgeschäft) abholen und ins Lager bringen. Im März des Folgejahres verlangt Agamemnon den Silbertisch zurück, den er der Tante zur Verwahrung gegeben hatte. Wem gehören (a) das Bett, (b) der Tisch?
cards.back:
(a) Bed: Nike — as heir Cato was owner; sale = IUSTA CAUSA; possession passed to Nike through Ganymed (IUSSUM or PECULIUM, ANIMO NOSTRO CORPORE ALIENO); RES NEC MANCIPI → civil-law ownership.
(b) Table: no derivative acquisition — the aunt was only a depositary, and Cato as heir merely steps into her position (NEMO PLUS IURIS …). But USUCAPIO by Nike: RES HABILIS (Cato sold in good faith, no FURTUM), title sale, BONA FIDES, possession since January, movable 1 year → completed by March of the following year (approx. 14 months) → Nike is owner; Agamemnon can no longer vindicate.

cards.topic: 10.11. Klausur 1 — Textbook exam cases (possession, acquiring ownership)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 7] Ago gives Brontes a sack of his own seed for safekeeping. Later, in Ago's flat, Brontes asks to be allowed to use the seed and promises to return a sack of the same quality after the harvest; Ago agrees. Possession and ownership over the course of events?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 7] Ago gibt Brontes einen Sack eigenes Saatgut zur Verwahrung. Später bittet Brontes in Agos Wohnung, das Saatgut verwenden zu dürfen, und verspricht, nach der Ernte einen Sack gleicher Qualität zurückzugeben; Ago stimmt zu. Besitz und Eigentum im Verlauf?
cards.back:
1. Deposit: Brontes detentor (natural possession), Ago mediate proprietary possessor and owner.
2. Agreement = loan for consumption (MUTUUM) of the seed: TRADITIO BREVI MANU — Ago gives up his intention to possess, Brontes henceforth holds in his own name; he already has CORPUS (Gaius D 41.1.9.5). The agreement need not be made in the presence of the thing.
3. Ownership: Ago owner + transfer of possession + IUSTA CAUSA (loan) → Brontes becomes owner; Ago has only a claim for the return of things of the same kind.

cards.topic: 10.11. Klausur 1 — Textbook exam cases (possession, acquiring ownership)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 9] The 12-year-old Secundus, without AUCTORITAS TUTORIS, sells and delivers his gold ring to Piso at a fair price paid immediately; Piso thinks he is 15. After 14 months the tutor demands the ring back. Must Piso hand it over? Variant: Secundus is 15, Piso only 13 — does Piso become owner?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 9] Der 12-jährige Secundus verkauft und übergibt Piso ohne AUCTORITAS TUTORIS seinen Goldring zu einem fairen, sofort bezahlten Preis; Piso hält ihn für 15. Nach 14 Monaten verlangt der Tutor den Ring zurück. Muss Piso ihn herausgeben? Variante: Secundus ist 15, Piso erst 13 — wird Piso Eigentümer?
cards.back:
Basic case: No. Derivative acquisition fails (a PUPILLUS cannot dispose without his tutor). But USUCAPIO: RES HABILIS; on acquisition from PUPILLI good faith suffices instead of a valid title; BONA FIDES through a mistake of fact about the age (Paulus D 41.4.2.15); 14 months > 1 year → Piso is owner.
Variant: Yes, derivatively — Secundus is of age; the minor Piso can conclude without a tutor transactions that only confer rights on him (the sale is a valid causa for his acquisition, NEGOTIUM CLAUDICANS); a PUPILLUS with sufficient maturity (INTELLECTUS) acquires possession himself (Paulus D 41.2.1.3).

cards.topic: 10.11. Klausur 1 — Textbook exam cases (possession, acquiring ownership)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 11] Ago instructs Bellona to exchange his horse for Carus' cow and hands the horse over to her. The next day Bellona meets Carus on his pasture; Carus agrees and hands the cow over to her. As regards the horse, Carus and Bellona agree that Bellona will hire it from Carus for four weeks. Possession and ownership of the horse?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 11] Ago beauftragt Bellona, sein Pferd gegen die Kuh des Carus zu tauschen, und übergibt ihr das Pferd. Am nächsten Tag trifft Bellona Carus auf seiner Weide; Carus willigt ein und übergibt ihr die Kuh. Für das Pferd vereinbaren Carus und Bellona, dass Bellona es vier Wochen von Carus mietet. Besitz und Eigentum am Pferd?
cards.back:
Possession: Ago possesses; on delivery to Bellona she becomes his detentor (Ago's mediate possession). Through the hire agreement Bellona henceforth holds the horse for Carus → CONSTITUTUM POSSESSORIUM: Carus acquires mediate possession, Bellona is now his detentor, Ago loses possession (his authorised detentor has transferred it).
Ownership: Bellona is authorised to dispose; exchange = causa aimed at transfer of ownership; transfer of possession by a tradition surrogate. Horse = RES MANCIPI → without MANCIPATIO Carus becomes only bonitarian owner (civil-law ownership after 1 year); Ago keeps the NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM.

cards.topic: 10.11. Klausur 1 — Textbook exam cases (possession, acquiring ownership)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 12] At the beginning of the year Victor sells a statue belonging to Euridike to Gaius, who is in good faith; the next day Gaius' slave Stilo collects it. Gaius gives it to Tiziana for safekeeping. In the middle of the year Gaius dies; his heir is Maevius, who collects the statue from Tiziana a year later. Shortly afterwards Euridike demands it back. Must Maevius hand it over?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 12] Victor verkauft Anfang des Jahres eine Statue der Euridike an den gutgläubigen Gaius; am nächsten Tag holt Gaius' Sklave Stilo sie ab. Gaius gibt sie Tiziana zur Verwahrung. Mitte des Jahres stirbt Gaius; Erbe ist Maevius, der die Statue nach einem Jahr von Tiziana holt. Kurz darauf verlangt Euridike sie zurück. Muss Maevius herausgeben?
cards.back:
No (if the statue is not stolen).
• No derivative acquisition (Victor not authorised).
• USUCAPIO: RES HABILIS — in case of doubt, assume the thing is not stolen (textbook note); title sale; Gaius' BONA FIDES at acquisition; possession through the slave (IUSSUM), then mediately through the detentor Tiziana — sufficient; Maevius continues as heir (SUCCESSIO IN POSSESSIONEM, his own good faith unnecessary); 1 year since acquisition has elapsed → Maevius is owner.
• If Victor knew that the statue belonged to another and sold it with intent to enrich himself, it would be a RES FURTIVA → no usucaption, REI VINDICATIO by Euridike.

cards.topic: 10.11. Klausur 1 — Textbook exam cases (possession, acquiring ownership)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 14] On 1 June Ramses buys ten beams from Iokaste for 500; they agree to select ten beams together at her timber yard on 15 June, which Ramses will then take away. On 7 June Ramses happens to drive past, enters the yard, selects ten beams and takes them away. Legal position?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 14] Ramses kauft am 1.6. bei Iokaste zehn Balken um 500; man vereinbart, am 15.6. auf ihrem Lagerplatz gemeinsam zehn Balken auszuwählen, die Ramses dann mitnimmt. Am 7.6. fährt Ramses zufällig vorbei, betritt den Lagerplatz, wählt zehn Balken und nimmt sie mit. Rechtslage?
cards.back:
• The contract of sale (1 June) gives rise only to claims; ownership passes only by TRADITIO.
• 7 June: no delivery — Iokaste does not participate, and a selection/delivery had been agreed only for 15 June → Ramses acquires possession unilaterally (originally), but not ownership.
• NEMO SIBI IPSE CAUSAM POSSESSIONIS MUTARE POTEST: taking possession on one's own initiative → no civil possession; according to Paulus D 41.2.5 a buyer who takes the purchased but undelivered thing without the seller's consent cannot usucapt.
• Iokaste remains owner (REI VINDICATIO); Ramses' possession is flawed in relation to her (CLAM) → no interdict protection against her. Ramses for his part has only the contractual claim to delivery.

cards.topic: 10.11. Klausur 1 — Textbook exam cases (possession, acquiring ownership)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 15] Irene sells Brontes the stallion Spartacus and the mare Junia; delivery after two weeks. Brontes then takes Spartacus and the mare Hera, which is very similar to Junia. Lucius had bought and paid for Spartacus from Irene months earlier but never received him. Legal position regarding (a) Spartacus, (b) Hera, (c) Junia?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 15] Irene verkauft Brontes den Hengst Spartacus und die Stute Junia; Übergabe nach zwei Wochen. Brontes nimmt dann Spartacus und die Junia sehr ähnliche Stute Hera mit. Lucius hatte Spartacus schon Monate zuvor von Irene gekauft und bezahlt, aber nie erhalten. Rechtslage bezüglich (a) Spartacus, (b) Hera, (c) Junia?
cards.back:
(a) Spartacus: double sale — ownership is acquired by whoever receives delivery first: Brontes (TRADITIO by the owner, sale). Horse = RES MANCIPI → Brontes bonitarian owner (Irene NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM). Lucius has only contractual claims against Irene.
(b) Hera: no causa (Junia was sold) → no acquisition of ownership; Brontes only possessor, Irene owner → REI VINDICATIO.
(c) Junia: ownership and possession remain with Irene; Brontes has the claim to delivery under the sale.

cards.topic: 10.11. Klausur 1 — Textbook exam cases (possession, acquiring ownership)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 16] Daphne inherits from her uncle Felix, among other things, a plot of land with a house which in fact belongs to Leo. On 1 May she sells and delivers it to Irene. In July Irene moves with her servants to her summer residence. At the beginning of August her neighbour Ares breaks in and moves in; two months later Irene returns and drives him out with the help of strong friends. On 1 June of the year after next Leo claims his property. Legal position on (a) 2 May, (b) 15 August, (c) 1 June of the year after next?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 16] Daphne erbt von Onkel Felix u.a. ein Grundstück mit Haus, das in Wahrheit Leo gehört. Am 1.5. verkauft und übergibt sie es an Irene. Im Juli zieht Irene samt Dienern in ihre Sommerresidenz. Anfang August bricht Nachbar Ares ein und zieht ein; zwei Monate später kehrt Irene zurück und vertreibt ihn mit kräftigen Freunden. Am 1.6. des übernächsten Jahres verlangt Leo sein Eigentum. Rechtslage am (a) 2.5., (b) 15.8., (c) 1.6. des übernächsten Jahres?
cards.back:
(a) 2 May: Leo owner; Irene possessor and usucapient in good faith (title sale, RES HABILIS — land cannot be stolen); as heir Daphne could not confer ownership (NEMO PLUS IURIS …).
(b) 15 August: Irene retains possession SOLO ANIMO; Ares does not acquire possession as long as Irene does not remain inactive or fail (Pomponius D 41.2.25.2; Ulpian D 41.2.6.1). Usucaption continues to run.
(c) Irene regains control → no change of possession, uninterrupted possession (force against Ares, whose possession is flawed, is permitted — VIM VI REPELLERE LICET). From 1 May to 1 June of the year after next > 2 years → Irene is owner by USUCAPIO; Leo's vindication fails.

cards.topic: 10.11. Klausur 1 — Textbook exam cases (possession, acquiring ownership)
cards.front: [Textbook Exam Case 22] In Brontes' house Ago sells him his horse Pegasus (inspected together on Ago's estate a week earlier) for 100.000; at the same time they agree that Ago will keep the horse for another year for a rent of 20.000. Possession and ownership of the horse?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exam Case 22] In Brontes' Haus verkauft Ago ihm sein Pferd Pegasus (vor einer Woche gemeinsam auf Agos Gut besichtigt) um 100.000; zugleich vereinbaren sie, dass Ago das Pferd noch ein Jahr gegen 20.000 Miete behält. Besitz und Eigentum am Pferd?
cards.back:
• Possession: CONSTITUTUM POSSESSORIUM — Brontes forms the intention to possess, Ago henceforth holds the horse for him as tenant → Brontes mediate proprietary possessor, Ago detentor. The inspection a week earlier did not by itself confer anything.
• Ownership: Ago owner + sale (IUSTA CAUSA) + transfer of possession by a tradition surrogate → transfer of ownership. Horse = RES MANCIPI → only bonitarian ownership (ACTIO PUBLICIANA); civil-law ownership after one year of possession — mediate possession through Ago suffices for usucaption.
